scenes.text: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth, and it's shrinking.
This swirling storm has raged since at least the eighteen hundreds.
It may even be over three hundred and fifty years old.
In the late eighteen hundreds, it was about forty one thousand kilometres long.
That's wide enough to line up about three Earths side by side.
When Voyager flew past in nineteen seventy nine, it was about one point eight Earths wide.
By twenty nineteen, NASA said it was down to about one point three Earths.
From twenty twelve, observers saw it shrink by about nine hundred kilometres a year.
It has also changed shape, from a long oval to something closer to a circle.
NASA's Juno spacecraft found the storm reaches more than two hundred kilometres down into Jupiter.
Scientists still aren't sure exactly why it is shrinking.
And nobody fully knows why its red colour gets stronger and fades over time.
Even now, it is still wider than the whole Earth.
Do you think the Great Red Spot will disappear in our lifetime?

title: Jupiter's giant storm is shrinking 🌪️
caption: Jupiter's Great Red Spot was about 3 Earths long in the late 1800s. By 2019 it was about 1.3 Earths wide, and scientists still aren't sure why it's shrinking.
